business: Moduo: an all-in-one workspace, pitched as a time-blocking planner built around finishing what you schedule
target: Knowledge workers and solo operators who time-block their day and have tried or paid for Motion, Sunsama, Morgen, Akiflow or Reclaim
where: Online; mostly US, UK and EU

segments.name: Employee at a startup or remote company

behaviours.name: Planner churner
behaviours.how: Has paid for two or three time-blocking apps and cancelled each after a few months.

behaviours.name: ADHD, tool-hopper
behaviours.how: Looks for apps that reduce guilt and decision load; drops anything that nags.

behaviours.name: Google Calendar purist
behaviours.how: Blocks time straight in Google Calendar and keeps tasks in a separate list.

behaviours.name: Price-sensitive
behaviours.how: Balks at $15-30/month planners and looks for a free tier first.

behaviours.name: Power user
behaviours.how: Wants keyboard shortcuts, integrations and automations before switching.

behaviours.name: Reads every review
behaviours.how: Checks Reddit and YouTube comparisons before trying anything.

objections: I've tried Motion and Sunsama; why would this one stick?
My calendar is Google or Outlook through work; will it really sync both ways?
I don't need email and contacts in my planner
No phone app means I can't check my plan on the go
Another subscription for something Google Calendar does for free
Planning apps make me feel guilty when I fall behind
habits: you plan tomorrow every evening and abandon the plan by 11am
you have a work Google Calendar and a personal iCloud one
you keep a running to-do list in Apple Notes
you cancelled a $20/month planner last quarter
_notes: Draws on PRODUCT_BRIEF.md section 3 (the execution gap) and .design/calendar/COMPETITIVE_RESEARCH.md (Morgen $15-30, Sunsama ~$20, Akiflow ~$19). Desktop Google/Outlook calendar OAuth isn't proven end-to-end yet, so the pitch doesn't promise it. Shares and incomes are guesses.
